segments.title: Where the letters appeared
segments.teaser: The small piece of scroll where the team reported finding letters.
segments.story: In September 2026 the Vesuvius Challenge team reported finding letters inside this scroll, and the spot they pointed to is on this little piece of papyrus. Nobody has unrolled it: what you see was revealed with X-rays and AI, on an ordinary computer.
segments.look: Look at the upper right. A row of curved strokes and a round shape stand out from the rest. Do they look like letters to you? Experts make the final call, but this is the kind of mark they look for.

segments.title: Wrap 58
segments.teaser: One full turn of the rolled-up scroll, about 4 × 7 cm, flattened out.
segments.story: Imagine unrolling one turn of a carpet. This is one turn of the scroll, traced and flattened by computer. Wraps 58, 60 and 62 sit right next to each other inside the roll, like neighbouring pages.
segments.look: Scan slowly across with the gold on. Look for rows of short strokes running in lines; lone blobs are usually just the papyrus itself.

segments.title: Wrap 60
segments.teaser: Two turns deeper into the same scroll.
segments.story: Two turns further into the roll from Wrap 58. The papyrus was squashed and baked by the volcano, so the writing is warped, but the ink can still survive.
segments.look: Try “Ink only” with “Dark letters on light” in More tools: it can look more like a page in a book.

segments.title: Wrap 62
segments.teaser: Another two turns in, with some of the clearest rows of marks.
segments.story: Another neighbour inside the roll. Some areas here show lines of marks that run side by side, the way writing does.
segments.look: Zoom into the upper middle and compare with the team's picture to see how much detail the full-size version keeps.

segments.title: The bright patch
segments.teaser: A smaller piece with strong, bold marks.
segments.story: This piece was traced automatically by the team's software. It has some of the boldest marks in the scroll, but bold doesn't always mean writing: cracks and fibres can light up too.
segments.look: Switch between “Gold highlight” and “Original scan”. Do the gold marks follow cracks in the papyrus, or do they cross them like pen strokes?

segments.title: The puzzle piece
segments.teaser: A wide piece full of activity. What do you see?
segments.story: A wide, busy piece. Treat it as a puzzle rather than a reading: the AI marks where ink might be, and people decide what is really writing.
segments.look: Use “Hide faint marks” in More tools to keep only the strongest gold, then look for shapes that repeat.
